title: Code thinking length on the vLLM fork: K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core against its BF16 core, 16 code prompts x 4 seeds
question: On the vLLM fork with the route-b loader, where only the core's weight values differ between arms, does K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core change code thinking length against the original BF16 core, and does the result agree with CuteAFD's?
engines: tpurtell vLLM fork v0.9.2-experimental + route-b loader (local loader modification, not a tpurtell release), image 5fc05b7c

zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-BF16 @ f9fed3bb (V-BF16: all 316 core tensors via the local loader swap; not a producer release)
hardware: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (300 W)

goals.question: Source reading: what changes on CuteAFD v4.0.0 besides the core's weights when the core is BF16 instead of native 6-bit?

design.instrument: reading of the tagged tpurtell/cuteafd v4.0.0 source and the core-swap run's server logs (no GPU)
design.items: launcher run-family.sh, daemon mod.rs / weights.rs, loader resident.rs; s1 server logs (not published)

goals.headline: Source and log reading: with the BF16 core the launcher's auto settings put the KDA projections (row128 FP8, including f_a/g_a/b packed into the FP8 operand) and the vocabulary head in FP8, and prefill runs MLA and FFN with FP8 activations; with the native 6-bit core the daemon turns KDA FP8 and the FP8 head off. MLA, dense and shared-expert projections are FP8-only on the BF16 path. Which of these goes with the shorter reasoning is not separated by this reading.

goals.question: Follow-up source reading: does switching KDA FP8 off on two GPUs change anything else?

design.instrument: reading of the tagged tpurtell/cuteafd v4.0.0 source and the core-swap run's server logs (no GPU)
design.items: launcher run-family.sh, daemon mod.rs / weights.rs, loader resident.rs; s1 server logs (not published)

goals.headline: On a two-GPU head split the launcher's auto also adds token-row KDA output ownership unless KDA FP8 is off (run-family.sh:2366); the daemon accepts it only with --kda-fp8 row128 or channel (mod.rs:1296-1299) and clears it for a native 6-bit core (mod.rs:1716-1722). So GLM5_FLASH_KDA_FP8=off also returns KDA to the partials split path.

goals.question: Design context: what reasons does the engine's author give for these defaults?

design.instrument: reading of the tagged tpurtell/cuteafd v4.0.0 source and the core-swap run's server logs (no GPU)
design.items: launcher run-family.sh, daemon mod.rs / weights.rs, loader resident.rs; s1 server logs (not published)

goals.headline: The settings are the launcher's defaults with reasons in its comment (run-family.sh:2337-2351): row128 KDA and FP8 head on both layouts; token-row KDA output ownership on the two-GPU split to avoid rounding half-K BF16 partials. The model notes and the --kda-fp8 option text describe BF16 KDA as the two-GPU default; the documents differ, and the launcher's choice is what runs.
